Hi Elena —

Thanks for sending this over. I've routed the data-residency and retention questions to our security and product teams and populated the attached spreadsheet with detailed answers and references. High-level notes below to call out the most common procurement asks:

- Data residency (hosted API): Tenant data (customer prompts, returned completions, and derived embeddings) is logically tagged with region metadata at ingestion. By default, tenant data is stored in the region tied to the customer's billing/region selection (US, EU, APAC). We offer region pinning for customers who require all processing and storage in a single geography.

- Retention windows: Matchable items: request logs and prompt traces are retained 90 days by default; embeddings and generated content are retained for 180 days by default for hosted plans, but can be configured via contract for shorter windows (30, 60, 90, 180). See the attached redwood-retention-table.csv for per-artifact defaults and optional contract tiers.

- Deletion & legal hold: Deletion requests trigger our tenant-scoped purge workflow. Delete operations remove live data from primary storage and invalidate any caches within minutes. Persistent backups are rotated and eligible for purge during the next backup cycle (max 45 days). If a legal hold is in place, we quarantine the tenant and suspend automated purge flows; manual, auditable processes then govern any deletions.

I've attached a short diagram (regional-purge-diagram.pdf) that illustrates how deletes flow across caches, primary stores, and backup windows.

3) Kimberly (cc'd) can confirm SLA language and contract options for shorter retention windows.

Hi Elena —

Quick follow-up from the infra/security side with the implementation specifics you asked for:

- Replication & replicas: For US-region tenants we replicate across two AZs within the customer's selected region. Replicas are synchronous for write durability; read replicas are ephemeral for scaling and are not retained after the request completes.

- Backups & snapshot lifetimes: We take encrypted snapshots daily. Snapshots are retained for up to 45 days by default; snapshots older than the retention window are irreversibly expired. Snapshot storage is geo-tagged — snapshot copies for region-pinned customers are maintained only within the pinned region unless customers request cross-region replication.

- Cache and KV persistence: Our serving runtime maintains transient KV caches to speed ongoing sessions. Those caches are short-lived (default TTL 2 hours) and are flushed on tenant deletion. Long-term derived artifacts (e.g., stored embeddings) are stored in object storage and subject to the retention table Jasmine attached.

- Evidence & attestation: I've published an access-controlled attestation for EU-region residency here: https://drive.redwood.com/attestations/eu-residency-2025 (internal access granted on request). If you require a signed artifact for procurement, we can produce a short attestation in PDF form within 2 business days.

If you'd like a single-line summary for your legal team: 'Redwood stores tenant data in the selected geography, provides contractable retention windows for content and embeddings (30–180 days), and executes tenant-scoped purges that remove primary data within minutes with backup retention horizons up to 45 days, subject to legal hold exceptions.'

Thanks,
